1.headline: A Record Number of People Come to Islands Near Africa
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Almost 2,000 people came to some islands in one day!
The islands are the Canary Islands. They are part of Spain. They are in the ocean near Africa. On Tuesday, 1,990 people came there on 15 boats. That is a new record.
Most boats came from Senegal and Gambia. These are countries in West Africa. The people want a better life. About 100 children were on the boats. One baby was born on the trip!
The trip is very dangerous. Many people have died at sea.
Spain has a big election this Sunday. Many voters care about this issue.
Again, a record number of people came to the Canary Islands in one day.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
하루 만에 거의 2,000명이 어떤 섬들에 왔습니다!
그 섬들은 카나리아 제도입니다. 스페인의 일부입니다. 아프리카 근처 바다에 있습니다. 화요일에 1,990명이 배 15척을 타고 그곳에 왔습니다. 새로운 기록입니다.
배 대부분은 세네갈과 감비아에서 왔습니다. 서아프리카에 있는 나라들입니다. 사람들은 더 나은 삶을 원합니다. 배에는 어린이 약 100명이 타고 있었습니다. 아기 한 명은 여행 중에 태어났습니다!
이 여행은 매우 위험합니다. 많은 사람이 바다에서 목숨을 잃었습니다.
스페인은 이번 일요일에 큰 선거가 있습니다. 많은 유권자가 이 문제에 관심이 많습니다.
다시 말해, 하루 만에 기록적인 수의 사람들이 카나리아 제도에 왔습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: Record Number of Migrants Reach Spain's Canary Islands
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
What happens when almost 2,000 people arrive on a small island in one day?

According to news reports, 1,990 migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands on Tuesday. Migrants are people who move to another country to live. They came on 15 boats. This is the biggest number ever for one day. Most of them landed on El Hierro, a small island with about 12,000 people.

The Canary Islands are part of Spain, but they are near West Africa. The local leader said most boats came from Senegal and Gambia. The sea was calm, and there was a full moon. About 100 children were on the boats. One baby was born during the trip.
The trip across the ocean is very dangerous. It can take days or weeks. Thousands of people have died on this route. This year, more than 26,000 people have arrived, and about half came in November.
This news comes at an important time. Spain has a national election this Sunday. Migration is a big issue for many voters.
To sum up, a record number of migrants reached the Canary Islands in one day.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
하루에 거의 2,000명이 작은 섬에 도착하면 어떤 일이 벌어질까요?
보도에 따르면 화요일에 이주민 1,990명이 스페인의 카나리아 제도에 도착했습니다. 이주민은 다른 나라로 옮겨 가 살려는 사람들입니다. 이들은 배 15척을 타고 왔습니다. 하루 기준으로 역대 가장 많은 숫자입니다. 대부분은 인구가 약 1만 2,000명인 작은 섬 엘이에로에 내렸습니다.
카나리아 제도는 스페인의 일부지만 서아프리카 가까이에 있습니다. 지역 지도자는 배 대부분이 세네갈과 감비아에서 왔다고 말했습니다. 바다는 잔잔했고 보름달이 떠 있었습니다. 배에는 어린이 약 100명이 타고 있었습니다. 아기 한 명은 이동 중에 태어났습니다.
바다를 건너는 이 여정은 매우 위험합니다. 며칠 또는 몇 주가 걸릴 수 있습니다. 이 경로에서 수천 명이 목숨을 잃었습니다. 올해 2만 6,000명이 넘게 도착했고, 그중 약 절반이 11월에 왔습니다.
이 소식은 중요한 시기에 나왔습니다. 스페인은 이번 일요일에 총선을 치릅니다. 이주는 많은 유권자에게 큰 문제입니다.
요약하면, 하루 만에 기록적인 수의 이주민이 카나리아 제도에 도착했습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: Record 1,990 Migrants Reach Spain's Canary Islands in One Day
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
How many people can one small island welcome in a single day? This week, Spain's Canary Islands found out.

According to news reports, 1,990 migrants arrived in the Canary Islands on Tuesday. A migrant is a person who moves to another country, often to find work or safety. Spain's sea rescue service said the people came on 15 boats. It was the most ever in one day. Rescue ships guided the boats, one after another, to El Hierro, a small island with about 12,000 people.

The Canary Islands belong to Spain, but they sit in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of West Africa. The regional leader, Fernando Clavijo, said most of the boats came from Senegal and Gambia. He said the sea was calm and there was a full moon. About 100 children were on the boats, including a baby who was born during the trip. He called it a historic and sad day.

This route is very dangerous. Trips can last days or even weeks, and thousands of people have died trying. More than 26,000 people have reached the islands this year, and about half of them came in November. Departures often rise in the autumn, before winter makes the sea rough.

Why does this matter now? Spain holds a national election this Sunday, and migration is a major issue for many voters. Leaders in the Canary Islands are also asking other parts of Spain to help care for children who arrived alone.
To sum up, a record 1,990 migrants reached Spain's Canary Islands in one day, just days before a national election.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
작은 섬 하나가 하루에 얼마나 많은 사람을 맞이할 수 있을까요? 이번 주 스페인의 카나리아 제도가 그 답을 알게 됐습니다.
보도에 따르면 화요일에 이주민 1,990명이 카나리아 제도에 도착했습니다. 이주민이란 흔히 일자리나 안전을 찾아 다른 나라로 옮겨 가는 사람을 말합니다. 스페인 해상 구조 당국은 이들이 배 15척을 타고 왔다고 밝혔습니다. 하루 기준 역대 최다입니다. 구조선들이 배를 한 척씩 차례로 인구 약 1만 2,000명의 작은 섬 엘이에로로 안내했습니다.
카나리아 제도는 스페인 땅이지만 대서양에서 서아프리카 해안 앞바다에 있습니다. 지역 수반인 페르난도 클라비호는 배 대부분이 세네갈과 감비아에서 왔다고 말했습니다. 바다가 잔잔했고 보름달이 떠 있었다고 했습니다. 배에는 이동 중에 태어난 아기를 포함해 어린이 약 100명이 타고 있었습니다. 그는 이날을 역사적이면서도 슬픈 날이라고 불렀습니다.
이 경로는 매우 위험합니다. 이동은 며칠, 길게는 몇 주가 걸릴 수 있고, 수천 명이 바다를 건너다 목숨을 잃었습니다. 올해 2만 6,000명이 넘는 사람이 이 섬들에 도착했고, 그중 약 절반이 11월에 왔습니다. 출발은 겨울이 바다를 거칠게 만들기 전인 가을에 자주 늘어납니다.
왜 지금 이 일이 중요할까요? 스페인은 이번 일요일에 총선을 치르는데, 이주는 많은 유권자에게 주요 문제입니다. 카나리아 제도의 지도자들은 또 혼자 도착한 아이들을 돌보는 데 스페인의 다른 지역들도 도와 달라고 요청하고 있습니다.
요약하면, 스페인 총선을 불과 며칠 앞두고 하루 만에 기록적인 1,990명의 이주민이 카나리아 제도에 도착했습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Canary Islands Record Nearly 2,000 Migrant Arrivals in a Single Day
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Nearly 2,000 people in a single day: that is the new record for migrant arrivals in Spain's Canary Islands.

According to Spain's maritime rescue service, 1,990 people reached the islands on Tuesday aboard 15 boats, the highest one-day total ever recorded there. Rescue vessels escorted the boats one after another into the small island of El Hierro, which has a population of only about 12,000.

The regional leader of the Canary Islands, Fernando Clavijo, told Spanish radio that most of the boats had set off from Senegal and Gambia. He said favorable sailing conditions and a full moon had encouraged departures. Around 100 minors were among the new arrivals, including a newborn baby delivered during the crossing. Clavijo described it as a historic but sad day, and he warned that El Hierro could not cope with such numbers on its own.

The Atlantic route to the Canaries is one of the deadliest migration routes in the world. Although the islands lie just over 100 kilometers from the African coast at their closest point, many boats take much longer routes to avoid patrols, and journeys can last for days or weeks. Thousands of people have died attempting the crossing. So far this year, more than 26,000 people have reached the islands, with roughly half arriving in November alone, as departures tend to peak before winter storms.

The timing is politically sensitive. Spain goes to the polls this Sunday in a national election, and migration has become a key concern for many voters. Meanwhile, island officials are urging other Spanish regions to share responsibility for unaccompanied minors.
To sum up, a record 1,990 migrants arrived in the Canary Islands in one day, putting fresh pressure on local services just days before Spain's national election.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.
하루에 거의 2,000명. 스페인 카나리아 제도의 이주민 도착 신기록입니다.
스페인 해상 구조 당국에 따르면 화요일에 1,990명이 배 15척에 나눠 타고 이 섬들에 도착했습니다. 이곳에서 기록된 하루 기준 역대 최다입니다. 구조선들은 배를 한 척씩 차례로 인구가 약 1만 2,000명에 불과한 작은 섬 엘이에로로 호위했습니다.

카나리아 제도 지역 수반 페르난도 클라비호는 스페인 라디오에 배 대부분이 세네갈과 감비아에서 출발했다고 말했습니다. 그는 항해하기 좋은 조건과 보름달이 출발을 부추겼다고 설명했습니다. 새로 도착한 사람 중에는 미성년자 약 100명이 있었고, 바다를 건너는 중에 태어난 신생아도 있었습니다. 클라비호는 이날을 역사적이지만 슬픈 날이라고 표현하며, 엘이에로 혼자서는 이런 인원을 감당할 수 없다고 경고했습니다.

카나리아 제도로 가는 대서양 경로는 세계에서 가장 치명적인 이주 경로 중 하나입니다. 섬들은 가장 가까운 지점에서 아프리카 해안과 100킬로미터 남짓 떨어져 있지만, 많은 배가 단속을 피하려고 훨씬 먼 길로 돌아가며 이동에 며칠에서 몇 주가 걸리기도 합니다. 수천 명이 바다를 건너다 목숨을 잃었습니다. 올해 지금까지 2만 6,000명이 넘게 도착했고, 그중 약 절반이 11월 한 달 동안 왔습니다. 겨울 폭풍 전에 출발이 정점에 이르는 경향이 있기 때문입니다.
시기도 정치적으로 민감합니다. 스페인은 이번 일요일 총선에서 투표를 하며, 이주는 많은 유권자의 핵심 관심사가 됐습니다. 한편 섬 당국자들은 보호자 없는 미성년자들에 대한 책임을 스페인의 다른 지역들도 나눠 져야 한다고 촉구하고 있습니다.
요약하면, 하루 만에 기록적인 1,990명의 이주민이 카나리아 제도에 도착해 스페인 총선을 며칠 앞두고 지역 행정에 새로운 부담을 주고 있습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

5.headline: Canary Islands Log Busiest Day on Record for Migrant Arrivals
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Spain's Canary Islands have just logged their busiest day on record for migrant arrivals, and the timing could hardly be more charged.

According to Spain's maritime rescue service, 1,990 people came ashore on Tuesday aboard 15 vessels, eclipsing a single-day record that had stood for only a matter of weeks. Search-and-rescue crews shepherded one dinghy after another into the port of La Restinga on El Hierro, the westernmost island of the archipelago and home to a mere 12,000 or so residents.

Fernando Clavijo, who heads the regional government, told Spanish radio that most of the boats had departed from Senegal and Gambia, spurred on by calm seas and a full moon. Roughly 100 minors were among those who arrived, including a four-day-old infant born during the voyage. Calling it a historic yet sorrowful day, Clavijo argued that European efforts in West Africa had failed to stem departures, since many people see leaving as their only path to work. He also pressed other Spanish regions to take in unaccompanied children, saying a small island like El Hierro simply cannot absorb an influx on this scale.

The Atlantic crossing is notoriously perilous. Although the nearest stretch of African coastline lies just over 100 kilometers away, smugglers often take circuitous routes to evade security forces, leaving passengers adrift for days or even weeks, and thousands have perished along the way. More than 26,000 people have reached the islands so far this year, with about half arriving in November, when departures typically surge ahead of rougher winter seas.

The spike lands on the eve of a national election on Sunday, in which migration ranks among voters' foremost concerns. The conservative opposition is seeking to unseat the Socialist-led government, and the far-right Vox party has made migration a centerpiece of its campaign.
To sum up, a record-breaking 1,990 migrants reached the Canary Islands in a single day, stretching local resources and thrusting the issue to the forefront days before Spain heads to the polls.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.
스페인 카나리아 제도에 이주민이 가장 많이 도착한 날이 새로 기록됐습니다. 그리고 시기도 이보다 더 민감할 수 없습니다.
스페인 해상 구조 당국에 따르면 화요일에 1,990명이 선박 15척을 타고 상륙해, 불과 몇 주 전에 세워진 하루 최다 기록을 넘어섰습니다. 수색 구조대는 고무보트를 한 척씩 차례로 엘이에로의 라 레스팅가 항구로 이끌었습니다. 엘이에로는 제도에서 가장 서쪽에 있는 섬으로, 주민이 1만 2,000명 남짓에 불과합니다.

지역 정부를 이끄는 페르난도 클라비호는 스페인 라디오에서, 배 대부분이 잔잔한 바다와 보름달에 힘입어 세네갈과 감비아에서 출발했다고 말했습니다. 도착한 사람 중 미성년자는 약 100명이었고, 항해 중에 태어난 생후 4일 된 아기도 있었습니다. 클라비호는 이날을 역사적이면서도 비통한 날이라 부르며, 많은 사람이 떠나는 것을 일자리를 얻는 유일한 길로 여기기 때문에 서아프리카에서의 유럽의 노력이 출발을 막지 못했다고 주장했습니다. 그는 또 엘이에로 같은 작은 섬은 이 정도 규모의 유입을 도저히 감당할 수 없다며, 스페인의 다른 지역들에 보호자 없는 아이들을 받아 달라고 압박했습니다.

대서양 횡단은 위험하기로 악명이 높습니다. 가장 가까운 아프리카 해안선은 100킬로미터 남짓 떨어져 있지만, 밀입국 알선업자들은 보안 당국을 피하려고 흔히 멀리 돌아가는 경로를 택해 승객들이 며칠, 길게는 몇 주씩 바다를 떠돌게 되고, 그 과정에서 수천 명이 목숨을 잃었습니다. 올해 지금까지 2만 6,000명이 넘는 사람이 이 섬들에 도착했으며, 그중 약 절반이 11월에 왔습니다. 11월은 겨울 바다가 거칠어지기 전에 출발이 대개 급증하는 때입니다.
이번 급증은 일요일 총선 바로 전에 일어났습니다. 이 선거에서 이주는 유권자들의 가장 큰 관심사 가운데 하나입니다. 보수 야당은 사회당이 이끄는 정부를 끌어내리려 하고 있고, 극우 정당 복스는 이주 문제를 선거 운동의 중심에 두고 있습니다.
요약하면, 기록적인 1,990명의 이주민이 하루 만에 카나리아 제도에 도착해 지역 자원을 압박하고, 스페인 총선을 며칠 앞두고 이 문제를 전면에 끌어올렸습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

items.ko: 카나리아 제도, 하루 이주민 최다 기록

1.headline: SpaceX Can Send One Million Satellites Into Space
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
One million new satellites? That is the plan!
SpaceX is a space company in the United States. On Wednesday, the government said yes to a big plan. SpaceX can send up to one million satellites into space.
The satellites will be like computers in the sky. They can help run AI. AI needs a lot of power. In space, there is a lot of sunlight.
Some people are worried. Scientists who study the stars do not like the plan. They worry about space trash.
This will take a long time. SpaceX has 14 years to finish.
Again, SpaceX wants one million satellites to work as computers in space.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
새 위성 100만 개요? 그게 바로 계획입니다!
스페이스X는 미국의 우주 기업입니다. 수요일에 정부가 큰 계획을 허락했습니다. 스페이스X는 위성을 최대 100만 개까지 우주로 보낼 수 있습니다.
이 위성들은 하늘에 떠 있는 컴퓨터 같은 역할을 합니다. AI를 돌리는 데 도움을 줄 수 있습니다. AI는 전력이 많이 필요합니다. 우주에는 햇빛이 많습니다.
걱정하는 사람들도 있습니다. 별을 연구하는 과학자들은 이 계획을 좋아하지 않습니다. 그들은 우주 쓰레기를 걱정합니다.
이 일은 오랜 시간이 걸릴 것입니다. 스페이스X에게는 끝내는 데 14년이 주어졌습니다.
다시 말해, 스페이스X는 위성 100만 개를 우주의 컴퓨터로 쓰고 싶어 합니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: SpaceX Gets a Yes for One Million Satellites
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
What if one million new satellites flew above the Earth?

A data center is a place full of powerful computers, like the ones that run artificial intelligence.

The plan is called Starmind. The satellites would fly between 500 and about 1,000 kilometers above Earth. They would mostly talk to each other with lasers. SpaceX has seven years to put its first working satellite in orbit, and 14 years to launch all of them.

They worry about space junk, crowded orbits and radio signals that could interfere with research. The head of the agency, Brendan Carr, said the decision opens a bold new frontier for computing.

4.headline: US Regulator Clears SpaceX Plan for a Million Data Center Satellites
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Elon Musk's SpaceX has won permission to put up to one million satellites into orbit, not to deliver internet service, but to process data for artificial intelligence.

On Wednesday, the US Federal Communications Commission granted conditional approval for the constellation, which SpaceX calls Starmind. The satellites would operate at altitudes of between 500 and roughly 1,000 kilometers and would communicate with one another mainly by laser, including links to the company's Starlink internet network.

Under the terms of the approval, SpaceX has seven years to place its first operational satellite in orbit and 14 years to complete the full constellation. However, regulators have not yet signed off on the company's plans for dealing with orbital debris for satellites flying above 600 kilometers.

The idea behind orbital data centers is to meet the soaring demand for computing power driven by AI, using solar energy collected in space. Still, the approval does not mean such facilities are coming soon. SpaceX must cut manufacturing and launch costs, find ways to cool processors in space, and pay for the chips it would send into orbit.

The plan drew objections from rivals and scientists. Amazon, which is building its own satellite network, described the proposal as a lofty ambition rather than a real plan. The American Astronomical Society raised concerns about space debris, crowded orbits, radio interference and possible environmental effects. The commission dismissed some of those concerns as falling outside its authority. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said the decision opens a bold new frontier for computing infrastructure.
Did you know? The first artificial satellite, the Soviet Union's Sputnik, was launched in 1957.
To sum up, SpaceX has conditional approval for up to one million data center satellites, though major technical and financial hurdles remain.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: SpaceX Cleared to Pursue a Million-Satellite Computing Network
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
A million satellites, each one a sliver of a vast computer in the sky: that is the vision US regulators have just cleared SpaceX to pursue.

On Wednesday, the Federal Communications Commission granted conditional approval for Starmind, a constellation of up to one million satellites designed to function as orbiting data centers. The spacecraft would circle the planet at altitudes ranging from 500 to roughly 1,000 kilometers, relaying data among themselves chiefly by laser and tying into the company's existing Starlink broadband network. Radio links would let engineers on the ground keep control if a satellite's primary systems failed.

The approval comes with strings attached. SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite aloft and 14 years to deploy the entire fleet. Regulators have yet to sign off on its debris-mitigation plans for satellites operating above 600 kilometers, and the company has sought a waiver from the rule requiring retired satellites in low orbit to reenter the atmosphere within five years.

The rationale is simple on paper: artificial intelligence is devouring electricity, and in orbit, solar power is abundant. Turning that vision into reality is another matter. SpaceX still has to drive down manufacturing and launch costs, work out how to shed heat from processors in the vacuum of space, and finance the chips it hopes to loft into orbit. The green light, in other words, hardly means orbital server farms are around the corner.

Critics were quick to weigh in. Amazon, a rival in the satellite internet business, dismissed the application as a lofty ambition rather than a real plan, while the American Astronomical Society warned of mounting debris, congested orbits, radio interference and environmental fallout. The commission brushed aside some objections, including threats to scientific research, as beyond its remit. Chairman Brendan Carr, for his part, hailed the move as opening a bold new frontier for computing.
Did you know? When Sputnik went up in 1957, it was the only artificial satellite in orbit.
To sum up, SpaceX has cleared a major regulatory hurdle for a million-satellite computing network, but the engineering and financial challenges ahead remain formidable.
Thank you for listening.

2.headline: Seoul Starts a Huge Housing Project Near Itaewon
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
How will Itaewon change when almost 6,000 new homes are built next to it?

The project will have 123 apartment buildings and 5,970 homes. Some buildings will be 21 floors high. About 1,020 homes will be for rent at lower prices. The work should finish in December 2030.

But some people feel sad. Many migrants and foreign residents lived on the hill because rent was cheap. The area is near Korea's first mosque. Now many halal restaurants and shops are closed. Some people say their community is gone.
To sum up, a huge housing project has started near Itaewon, and the neighborhood will change a lot.

이 사업으로 아파트 123개 동, 5,970가구가 들어섭니다. 일부 건물은 21층 높이가 됩니다. 약 1,020가구는 더 낮은 가격에 임대됩니다. 공사는 2030년 12월에 끝날 예정입니다.
이 계획은 20년도 더 전인 2003년에 시작됐습니다. 이 지역은 가파른 언덕에 있고, 많은 집이 아주 낡았습니다. 오세훈 시장은 그곳 사람들에게 더 좋은 집이 필요했다고 말했습니다.
하지만 슬퍼하는 사람들도 있습니다. 집세가 싸서 많은 이주민과 외국인 주민이 이 언덕에 살았습니다. 이 지역은 한국 최초의 이슬람 사원 근처에 있습니다. 지금은 많은 할랄 식당과 가게가 문을 닫았습니다. 자신들의 공동체가 사라졌다고 말하는 사람들도 있습니다.
요약하면, 이태원 근처에서 거대한 주택 사업이 시작됐고, 이 동네는 많이 바뀔 것입니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: Work Begins on Seoul's Biggest Redevelopment, Next to Itaewon
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
What happens to a neighborhood's character when almost six thousand new homes are built on top of it?

According to The Korea Herald, construction officially began on Thursday on the Hannam District 3 redevelopment project in Yongsan, Seoul. Redevelopment means tearing down old buildings and building new ones. The Seoul city government and Hyundai Engineering and Construction call it the largest redevelopment project in the city's history.

The plan is huge. It covers 386,000 square meters near Itaewon. There will be 123 apartment buildings up to 21 floors high, with 5,970 homes. Of these, 1,020 will be public rental homes, which means homes that the government rents out at lower prices. The project aims to finish by December 2030.

The area was chosen for redevelopment back in 2003, more than 20 years ago. It sits on a steep hill, and many houses were old. At the ceremony, Mayor Oh Se-hoon said better housing was badly needed. He also said some parts of the land are up to 58 meters higher than others.

But there is another side to the story. The hill was once home to people with low incomes, including many migrants and foreign residents. It lies just below the Seoul Central Mosque, Korea's first mosque. Now, many halal restaurants, grocery stores and bars have closed. Some longtime residents say the community has been scattered.
To sum up, Seoul has started building nearly 6,000 homes in Hannam, and people are asking what will happen to Itaewon's diverse identity.
Thank you for listening.

코리아헤럴드에 따르면 목요일 서울 용산의 한남3구역 재개발 사업이 공식적으로 착공했습니다. 재개발이란 낡은 건물을 허물고 새 건물을 짓는 것을 말합니다. 서울시와 현대건설은 이를 서울 역사상 가장 큰 재개발 사업이라고 부릅니다.
계획의 규모는 엄청납니다. 이태원 근처 38만 6,000제곱미터에 걸쳐 있습니다. 최고 21층 높이의 아파트 123개 동에 5,970가구가 들어섭니다. 이 가운데 1,020가구는 공공임대주택으로, 정부가 더 낮은 가격에 빌려주는 집을 말합니다. 사업은 2030년 12월까지 마무리하는 것이 목표입니다.
이 지역은 20년도 더 전인 2003년에 재개발 지역으로 지정됐습니다. 가파른 언덕에 자리해 있고 많은 집이 낡았습니다. 착공식에서 오세훈 시장은 더 나은 주거가 절실히 필요했다고 말했습니다. 또 땅의 일부는 다른 곳보다 최대 58미터나 높다고 말했습니다.

요약하면, 서울이 한남에서 6,000가구 가까운 집을 짓기 시작했고, 사람들은 이태원의 다양한 정체성이 어떻게 될지 묻고 있습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Seoul Breaks Ground on Its Largest Redevelopment as Itaewon Faces Change
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Seoul has broken ground on the largest redevelopment project in its history, and it could reshape one of the city's most diverse neighborhoods.

According to The Korea Herald, construction officially began on Thursday at Hannam District 3 in Yongsan, next to the Itaewon area. The site covers 386,000 square meters and will eventually hold 123 apartment buildings of up to 21 stories, with a total of 5,970 homes, including 1,020 public rental units. The project is scheduled for completion by December 2030.

The hillside neighborhood was designated for redevelopment as far back as 2003, but steep terrain and aging housing slowed progress for more than two decades. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony, Mayor Oh Se-hoon said improving the residential environment was urgently needed, noting that parts of the site differ in elevation by as much as 58 meters. District 3 is the first of four active redevelopment zones in the wider Hannam New Town to begin construction, and a neighboring district is expected to follow in the second half of 2027.

However, the project is also changing the character of the area. For decades, the hill offered relatively affordable housing to migrants, foreign residents and low-income families. It lies directly below the Seoul Central Mosque, the country's first mosque, and was known for halal restaurants, small family businesses and nightlife venues. Many of those storefronts are now shuttered. Some residents told the newspaper that the community has been torn apart as people moved away, while one longtime resident said it felt remarkable to see the neighborhood completely transformed.
To sum up, work has begun on nearly 6,000 new homes in Hannam, raising questions about how Itaewon's multicultural identity will survive the change.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Seoul's Biggest-Ever Redevelopment Breaks Ground Beside Itaewon
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Seoul has just broken ground on the most ambitious redevelopment in its history, and the bulldozers are bringing a familiar question with them: what becomes of a neighborhood's soul when its streets are rebuilt from scratch?

According to The Korea Herald, construction formally got underway on Thursday at Hannam District 3, a sprawling 386,000-square-meter hillside site in Yongsan that borders Itaewon. When complete, slated for December 2030, it will comprise 123 apartment blocks of up to 21 stories and 5,970 homes, 1,020 of them public rental units. The city government and Hyundai Engineering and Construction have billed it as the largest redevelopment project Seoul has ever undertaken.

It has been a long time coming. The area was earmarked as a New Town district in 2003, only for steep terrain and dilapidated housing to stall progress for more than two decades. At the groundbreaking ceremony, Mayor Oh Se-hoon acknowledged the scale of the challenge, pointing out that elevations across the site vary by as much as 58 meters, while stressing that an upgrade to living conditions was long overdue. District 3 is the first of four active zones in the broader Hannam New Town to break ground, with a neighboring district targeting the second half of 2027.

Yet the transformation carries a cost that is harder to measure. The hillside, once a low-income enclave, drew migrants and foreign residents with its affordable rents and its proximity to the Seoul Central Mosque, the country's first. Halal eateries, grocery stores, family-run shops and nightlife venues gave the area its eclectic character. Many of those storefronts now sit shuttered, and some residents say the community has been scattered to the winds. Others, including a longtime member of the redevelopment association, marvel at how thoroughly the neighborhood is being remade.
To sum up, work has begun on nearly 6,000 homes in Hannam, and while the future skyline is taking shape, the fate of Itaewon's distinctive multicultural identity remains an open question.
Thank you for listening.
